target: Ero appena arrivato quando è iniziato a piovere.
english: I had just arrived when it started raining.
tip: Arrivare forms its past with essere, so ero appena arrivato is literally I was just arrived where English says I had just arrived.

target: Credevo che la banca fosse aperta il sabato.
english: I believed the bank was open on Saturday.
tip: Il before a weekday means 'every': il sabato, on Saturdays as a habit; drop il for one specific Saturday.

target: Pareva che la pioggia non volesse smettere mai.
english: It seemed the rain would never stop.
tip: Italian keeps the double negative: non volesse smettere mai literally says 'not... never', meaning would never stop.

target: Se il museo fosse aperto, lo visiteremmo oggi.
english: If the museum were open, we'd visit it today.
tip: Object pronouns sit before a conjugated verb: lo visiteremmo, we'd visit it, not visiteremmo lo.

target: Se non costasse così tanto, comprerei quel vestito.
english: If it didn't cost so much, I'd buy that dress.
tip: Così before an adverb or adjective means 'so': costasse così tanto, cost so much.

target: Se non avessi dimenticato il passaporto, saresti partito.
english: If I hadn't forgotten my passport, I would have left.
tip: Unreal past 'if': se plus the pluperfect subjunctive, then the past conditional: se avessi dimenticato, saresti partito.

target: Se mi chiami, vengo a prenderti alla stazione.
english: If you call me, I'll come pick you up at the station.
tip: Italian often uses the present for a certain near future: se mi chiami, vengo, means I'll come.

target: Non dimenticherò mai quello che hai fatto per me.
english: I'll never forget what you did for me.
tip: Quello che means 'what' in the sense of 'the thing that': quello che hai fatto, what you did.

target: Avevano lavorato insieme per dieci anni prima di litigare.
english: They had worked together for ten years before quarreling.
tip: Prima di is followed by the infinitive, not a conjugated verb: prima di litigare, before quarreling.

target: Poiché il ristorante era pieno, abbiamo cenato a casa.
english: Since the restaurant was full, we had dinner at home.
tip: Poiché means 'since' or 'because', giving a reason, and takes the indicative: poiché era pieno, since it was full.

target: Se domani fa bello, portiamo i bambini al parco.
english: If the weather is nice tomorrow, let's take the kids to the park.
tip: Weather uses fare: fa bello means the weather is nice, literally 'it makes nice'.

target: Se avessi studiato di più da giovane, ora sarei preparato.
english: If I had studied more when young, I'd now be prepared.
tip: You can mix time frames: se avessi studiato is a past condition, but ora sarei preparato gives a present result.

target: Bisogna fare attenzione.
english: One must pay attention.
tip: Bisogna never takes a subject; the one must sense is built into the verb: bisogna fare attenzione = one must pay attention.

target: Penso che lui abbia ragione.
english: I think he's right.
tip: The subjunctive is triggered by 'penso che' (I think that).

target: Bisogna che tu parta subito.
english: You need to leave right away.
tip: Use bisogna che plus the subjunctive when the need targets a specific person: bisogna che tu parta subito.

target: Prima che tu parta, salutami.
english: Before you leave, say goodbye to me.
tip: 'Prima che' always requires the subjunctive.

target: Credo che sia una buona idea.
english: I think it's a good idea.
tip: Sia is the subjunctive of essere, triggered by 'credo che'.

target: Voglio che tu venga alla festa.
english: I want you to come to the party.
tip: English says I want you to come, but Italian cannot use an infinitive across two subjects: it needs voglio che tu venga.

target: Se avessi più tempo, viaggerei di più.
english: If I had more time, I'd travel more.
tip: For unreal ifs, se takes the imperfect subjunctive (avessi) and the result clause uses the conditional (viaggerei), not the future.

target: Venne a sapere la verità troppo tardi.
english: He found out the truth too late.
tip: Venire a sapere is literally to come to know, and it means to find out: venne a sapere la verità = he found out the truth.

target: La porta viene chiusa alle sei di sera.
english: The door is closed at six in the evening.
tip: Viene chiusa is a passive with venire that stresses the event happening; essere, la porta è chiusa, would describe a state instead.

target: La medicina va presa dopo i pasti.
english: The medicine must be taken after meals.
tip: andare plus a past participle, va presa, makes a passive of obligation: va presa means must be taken, not just is taken.

target: Spende come se avesse milioni in banca.
english: He spends as if he had millions in the bank.
tip: come se, meaning as if, needs the subjunctive: come se avesse (imperfect), never the indicative come se ha.

target: Se ti chiede scusa, perdonalo.
english: If he apologizes, forgive him.
tip: Affirmative commands attach the object pronoun to the verb's end: perdona plus lo becomes perdonalo, forgive him.

target: In Italia si mangia bene.
english: In Italy people eat well.
tip: 'Si' impersonal: si + third person for general statements.

target: Qui si vendono prodotti locali.
english: Local products are sold here.
tip: "Si" passivante with plural: verb agrees with the noun. "Si vendono case" = Houses are sold. The noun is the grammatical subject.

target: Voleva sapere quando saremmo partiti.
english: He wanted to know when we would leave.
tip: To say 'would' from a past viewpoint, Italian uses the past conditional: saremmo partiti means we would leave.

target: Le email vengono controllate ogni mattina.
english: Emails are checked every morning.
tip: In the passive, venire can replace essere to stress the ongoing action: vengono controllate means are checked.

target: Se fossi te, lo farei senza pensarci.
english: If I were you, I'd do it without thinking.
tip: The se-clause takes the subjunctive fossi, never the conditional: it is se fossi te, and se sarei is the classic mistake.

target: La verità va detta, anche quando è scomoda.
english: The truth must be told, even when it's uncomfortable.
tip: andare plus a past participle expresses obligation: va detta means must be told, not is going.
